series: Things Living In Your House, Part 41
sources: CDC, About Bed Bugs: 1-7 mm (about Lincoln's head on a penny); bite marks can take up to 14 days to develop in some people; bed bugs can travel over 100 feet in a night but tend to live within 8 feet of where people sleep; rusty-colored blood spots, a sweet musty odor; not known to spread disease; https://www.cdc.gov/bed-bugs/about/index.html

Univ. of Kentucky Entomology, Bed Bugs (ENTFACT-636, M. Potter): 1-4 months without feeding in heated buildings, a year or longer at 55 F or less; lifespan about 10 months; eggs hatch in about a week; can mature in a month at 70-80 F; about 30 percent of people do not react even when bitten repeatedly; fit crevices no wider than a toothpick; crawl room to room and floor to floor via cracks; dark spotting and tan shed skins; laundering 120 F minimum or a dryer at medium-high heat 10-20 minutes; freezing takes one to two weeks; https://entomology.mgcafe.uky.edu/ef636

Kells, S. (Univ. of Minnesota), Heat treatment for bed bugs, EPA-hosted presentation: 118 F lethal to adults (about 20 min), eggs need about 90 min, 122 F for eggs; https://archive.epa.gov/epa/sites/production/files/2014-06/documents/12-kellsheat.pdf

title: 100 Feet a Night to Your Bed 🩸 (Things Living In Your House #41)
tiktok_caption: bed bugs in your bed 🩸 they can crawl over 100 feet in a night to reach you, and the bite can take 14 days to show up. Checking your mattress tonight? 🛏️ yes / 🙈 no #bedbugs #bedbugbites #bugsinyourbed #meatballmyths

beats.say: Something can crawl 100 feet tonight, just to reach your bed.
It finds you. It bites. And it leaves no mark.
For some people, the bite takes 14 days to show up.
And about 3 in 10 people never react at all.
So you could have them, and never know.
It fits in a crack no wider than a toothpick.
It crawls room to room, and floor to floor, through cracks in your walls.
But it likes to live within 8 feet of where you sleep.
Look for rusty blood spots on your mattress.
Dark specks, which are its dried poop. And tan, empty skins.
Some people smell it, too. Sweet, and musty.
A female lays eggs every day. They hatch in about a week.
In a warm house, a baby can grow up in a month.
Starve it out? In a heated home, it can wait months.
Below about 55 degrees, it can wait a year or longer.
Adults are about the size of Lincoln's head on a penny.
So what kills it? Heat.
At 118 degrees, adults die in about 20 minutes.
Wash your sheets hot, then dry them on high for 20 minutes.
Freezing works too. But it takes one to two weeks.
The good news? It's not known to spread disease.
Just itchy bites. From a bug that, tonight,
